items.label: Observation
items.definition: Observation names what can be encountered or measured without already accepting DOT. Experience occurs. Reports vary with attention. Neural injury can alter memory, perception, personality, and responsiveness. Institutions can shape the options available to a person. These observations require interpretation, but they are not unique predictions of this theory.

items.label: External model
items.definition: External model names an account developed in an established field and used here within its proper domain. Predictive processing, memory systems, interoception, threat learning, decoherence, and cosmological parameter estimation belong at this level. Their inclusion does not imply that their authors endorse DOT.

items.label: DOT derivation
items.definition: DOT derivation names a claim that follows from the theory’s postulates. If Big C differentiates Little c and Little c participates in a rule-bound Reality Frame through an Avatar, then the body is an interface rather than the producer of the experiencer. This conclusion may be internally required by DOT while remaining externally unverified.

items.label: Speculative extension
items.definition: Speculative extension names a possibility that the current architecture suggests but does not yet derive or test adequately. Claims about consciousness beyond biological death, communication across Reality Frames, or Intent changing quantum outcomes belong here unless and until a mechanism and discriminating evidence are supplied.

argument.text: DOT provides the organizing lens. Documentary records establish particular events and practices. Illustrative situations show how a proposed mechanism might operate. Ethical commitments state what this book believes people owe one another. These forms of reasoning have different jobs.
argument.section: What Kind of Argument This Is

argument.text: A record of exploitation does not establish that consciousness is independent of the brain. A moving experience does not establish Big C. A useful description of learned behavior does not establish DOT's speculative account of T × E. Those questions require their own arguments and evidence. Applying DOT to culture cannot settle them by moral urgency.
argument.section: What Kind of Argument This Is

argument.text: Equally, a person's disagreement with DOT is not evidence of fear, domination, or infection. Readers can question the framework and still examine the practical relationships described here. A serious school of thought must permit its own claims to be corrected.
argument.section: What Kind of Argument This Is

argument.text: The situations presented without a named documentary source are illustrative, not reports of interviews or measured national patterns. Historical and research references support the limited claims attached to them. They do not establish the prevalence of every mechanism proposed in the book.

argument.text: The ethical standard remains direct: every person has standing; power carries obligations; claims should be open to evidence; and those affected by consequential decisions need a meaningful way to seek correction. This standard applies to governments and businesses, families and movements, critics and founders. It also applies to this manifesto.

definition.text: Exclusively the attitude that treats domination of other people as a legitimate route to security, worth, or advantage. People can adopt or resist it; institutions can organize or reward it. The term does not identify a person, class, nation, ethnicity, or separate organism.

Consequential control that subordinates others' agency to securing one's own position, or that of a favored group or institution, while withholding adequate justification, meaningful challenge, or reciprocal accountability. A justified, proportionate, reviewable constraint is not automatically domination.
Rules, incentives, dependencies, or practices that organize and protect the exercise of that attitude. Its presence requires evidence about a particular arrangement.

In this argument, benefit secured through unjustified imposed costs or exploitation of dependence, particularly where effective challenge is obstructed. Payment, profit, wealth, and intermediation do not establish it by themselves.

The living public and conditions of shared life. Membership is not earned through economic contribution, citizenship, social rank, or agreement with this book. The metaphor does not imply one collective consciousness or a single national will.

The function through which delegated authority and interpretive credibility direct shared activity. It can enable correction or protect a harmful arrangement. It does not assign a profession or a community a fixed moral nature.
A metaphor for learning, internalizing, and reproducing the attitude of dominance. It is not a pathogen, clinical diagnosis, or inference justified by disagreement or distress.
In DOT, the persistent capacity to carry and update state for a local instance of awareness. DOT's stronger claim that this capacity is not exhausted by biology remains unverified.

The accumulated organization of Canvas state: meanings, expectations, fears, loyalties, habits, skills, and other carried patterns. The Painting is not the Canvas itself or the entirety of the experiencer.
A directional commitment that selects or stabilizes a move toward action. It is distinct from every thought, urge, or response that appears before commitment.
The relatively stable policy of action expressed through repeated interpretation and response. It can be revised; it is not a permanent measure of intrinsic human worth.

Meaningful actions both available and visible under present bodily, psychological, relational, and structural conditions. Material impossibility cannot be repaired solely by noticing another interpretation.

Lower-case fear names a protective signal or state related to predicted threat. Capital Fear names threat becoming the governing organizer of interpretation and decision-space. The distinction concerns governance, not intensity alone.

At the human level in DOT, the condition and practice in which Fear no longer governs: accurate contact, truthful revision, proportionate boundaries, concern for others' agency, accountability, and repair. It does not require appeasement, reconciliation, or absence of fear.

Noticing a bodily state or learned pattern without automatically identifying with or obeying it. The living body and Canvas remain functionally coupled. This practice does not establish DOT's ontological claims.

The ethical narrowing through which truth, care, agency, and responsibility become subordinate to protecting advantage or position. It describes a proposed pattern of conduct, not a mental illness or measured national condition.
Deliberate, answerable participation in shaping responses and shared conditions within real constraints. It is not independence from history, other people, the body, or consequence.

intro.text: A serious claim about dominance should follow a complete enough relationship to be challenged.

text.text: Begin with the power: who can decide what? Distinguish ownership, delegated authority, professional influence, and simple participation. A person may benefit from an arrangement without being able to set its terms.

prompt.text: Begin with the power: who can decide what?

text.text: Then identify the dependence. What does the affected person need? Which alternatives exist in practice? What would leaving, appealing, or refusing cost? Do not infer captivity from every inconvenience or freedom from every theoretical alternative.

prompt.text: Then identify the dependence. What does the affected person need? Which alternatives exist in practice? What would leaving, appealing, or refusing cost?

text.text: Next identify the benefit and the imposed burden. Money is one benefit, but status, discretion, secrecy, and protection from criticism can matter too. A burden may fall on people absent from the contract, including families, neighboring communities, or future participants.

prompt.text: Next identify the benefit and the imposed burden.

text.text: Then examine justification and correction. What legitimate purpose does the restriction serve? Is it proportionate? Who can test the reason? What happens when the reason fails? A remedy dependent entirely upon the goodwill of the original decision-maker may be inadequate where the stakes and asymmetry are substantial.

prompt.text: Then examine justification and correction. What legitimate purpose does the restriction serve? Is it proportionate? Who can test the reason? What happens when the reason fails?

text.text: Finally, examine response to evidence. A mistake followed by prompt repair differs from a known injury concealed for advantage. A person constrained by a rule differs from one who can revise it and chooses not to. Responsibility must follow these distinctions.

counter.text: This method also identifies counterevidence. Realistic exit, independent review, effective protections against retaliation, transparent allocation of costs, and documented correction can weaken a particular claim of domination. They do not need to make an institution perfect to matter. An analysis that cannot recognize improvement has become a closed explanation.

weaken.text: A framework earns trust partly by specifying what it cannot claim.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

weaken.text: If a person complies with a harmful demand while openly distinguishing necessity from endorsement, that weakens the claim that they have internalized dominance. If an institution protects criticism and changes a rule after credible evidence, that weakens the claim that its purpose is insulated from correction. If a restriction is justified, proportionate, reviewable, and responsive to the people affected, the mere presence of authority does not establish domination.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

weaken.text: If someone rejects this analysis for reasons that survive scrutiny, rejection is counterargument, not a symptom. The account cannot become self-sealing by declaring that anyone who denies infection has proved its depth.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

weaken.text: An inference about fear also requires evidence. A person's conduct may support an interpretation of what they are protecting, but that interpretation remains revisable. Reward, convention, incomplete knowledge, institutional constraint, and a genuine competing obligation can provide other explanations. A serious account must consider them.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

weaken.text: The most reliable practical conclusion is often narrower than the most satisfying moral story. We may know that a procedure punishes justified objection without knowing the complete psychology of its designers. That can be enough to require changing the procedure. Accountability need not wait for access to a hidden interior.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

weaken.text: Precision strengthens the critique. It prevents the language of cultural analysis from becoming a claim to read minds. It also allows cooperation among people who disagree about ultimate explanations but can recognize a documented harm and a workable remedy.
weaken.section: 17. What Would Weaken the Infection Account?

change.text: The success of this argument cannot be measured by how many people repeat its vocabulary. Calling a habit a Painting does not establish that it has been revised. Calling an organization humane does not establish that participants can challenge it.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: At the personal level, ask what happens in a recurring situation where dominance previously appeared. Can a person notice the governing interpretation? Can they distinguish a feeling from a fact and a draft from a commitment? Do they respond differently when it matters? When they fail, do they acknowledge the consequence and make a specific repair?
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: At the relational level, ask whether other people have more room to speak accurately, set a reasonable boundary, and receive an explanation. Their accounts matter, particularly when they have less power. A leader's self-assessment cannot stand in for the experience of those affected.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: At the institutional level, ask whether justified concerns reach someone who can act, whether retaliation is prevented and addressed, whether errors produce remedies, and whether repeated failures change incentives or rules. A record of correction is more informative than the existence of a policy alone.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: These are directions for evaluation, not a newly validated measurement scale. Any assessment needs appropriate evidence and safeguards. It should avoid turning private distress into a public score or collecting intimate information merely because the framework has named an inner process.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: We also need to ask who has become less free. A reform can shift burdens to people outside its field of view. A convenient digital alternative can create a new gatekeeper. A protective rule can be used selectively. The inquiry must follow the consequence beyond the circle that celebrates the change.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: Progress will be uneven. Some practices can improve while others remain harmful. Recognizing a real improvement is not surrender; it is necessary to accurate judgment. Recognizing persistent harm is not disloyalty; it is necessary to the same standard.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing

change.text: The practical measure is whether people gain truthful, meaningful possibility under conditions that remain answerable. That measure can guide work without pretending the work has already been completed.
change.section: 12. How We Know Whether Anything Is Changing
